claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He lives at home with me and I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of his exact age at the moment - he's somewhere in his mid to late teens, between 15 and 19. Is that going to be a problem for figuring out if I'm eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That age range is important because the eligibility rules change at age 16. Let me ask you this:

**Is Alex under 16, or is he 16 or older?** 

If he's 16 or older, I'll also need to know whether he's staying in approved education or training (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, T-levels, or certain vocational courses).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 16 or older, definitely. He's still in education - doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 16 or older and in approved education (A-levels), that's good for eligibility purposes.

Now I need to ask about your living situation:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is Alex under 20 years old?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now I need to check a couple more things:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great. Just a few final questions:

**Does Alex work 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work that much - he's focused on his studies. And he's not receiving any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also check one final thing:

**Is Alex living with you at home, or does he live somewhere else (for example, in student accommodation, with another relative, or in care)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the criteria:

✓ Alex is under 20 years old  
✓ He's in approved education (A-levels)  
✓ He lives at home with you in the UK  
✓ He's not working 24+ hours per week  
✓ He's not claiming benefits in his own right  
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have some of it back through tax.

If you'd like to proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you can make a claim through the government's official channels.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
